channel.title: Space Digest
channel.description: The podcasts worth your week, in a minute each.

item.title: Too Big to Fire: Jensen Huang Is Back as Nvidia CEO
item.description: Nvidia’s CEO returned after Washington said he posed no security risk, raising fears that AI companies are now too important to challenge.

item.title: The One-Person Biotech | OpenAI Life Sciences
item.description: AI may turn drug research from a chain of bottlenecks into a process that can learn continuously.

item.title: A Deep Dive Into Just War Theory (Dr. Alex Plato) | Ep. 606
item.description: A just war can begin morally—and still become evil when its methods cross the line.

item.title: #359 Colby Adcock - What If One Soldier Could Command an Entire Drone Swarm?
item.description: A startup wants one human to command millions of cooperating machines, but admits friend-or-foe identification remains unsolved.

item.title: 327. From Rushing Through to Locking In: Finding Meaning at Work
item.description: The fastest way through work may be to slow down, find who it serves, and choose how to do it well.

item.title: When AI Labs Rival Nations
item.description: AI labs may soon need the accountability of governments, while AI itself could decide how people work and live.

item.title: Replay: How the Internet Happened | Chris Dixon & Brian McCullough (2018)
item.description: The internet’s biggest breakthroughs often won because they were simple, timely, and convenient—not perfect.

item.title: The Professional Network Built for You and Your AI Agent
item.description: The next professional network may be built around trusted proof of work, with AI agents searching it for you.

item.title: Why You Should Try Gemini Neon (Even if You Love Fable)
item.description: Gemini Neon’s biggest advantage may not be winning benchmarks, but thinking unlike ChatGPT and Claude.

item.title: Why the Agent Era Needs a New Operating System | DHH
item.description: AI agents could turn Linux’s old flaws into its greatest strengths—and let tiny teams build what once took entire companies.

item.title: #2584 - Mike Baker
item.description: The episode argues that America’s biggest threats may arrive quietly—through compromised systems, institutions, and incentives.

item.title: We Need to Talk About Trent Horn + a BIG Announcement
item.description: Trent Horn’s unexplained departure sparks praise, caution, and a closer look at faith beyond the headlines.

item.title: The 10 Biggest Days in AI History
item.description: AI’s biggest turning points came from surprises, rivalries, and one chatbot released with almost no expectations.

item.title: Malcolm Guite Ranks the Greatest Novels of All Time | Last Call Ep. 41
item.description: Great books do more than entertain: they train the imagination to see faith, evil, desire, and freedom differently.

item.title: How Fast Should We Build Superintelligence? | Nick Bostrom
item.description: Superintelligence may deserve a short delay—but waiting too long could cost millions of lives and humanity’s future.

item.title: #358 Ed Barnhart - Inside America’s Forgotten Pyramid Civilization
item.description: America’s first cities grew from burial grounds, shell waste and trade—not just farming or conquest.

item.title: #2583 - Bob Gymlan
item.description: The episode treats alien sightings, ancient mysteries, and AI as clues to a future humans may be building blindly.

item.title: Why the AI Kids Hate Astra 6.2
item.description: A model launch that looked broken to coders may reveal OpenAI is chasing cheaper, broader workplace use.

item.title: The Missing Layer for Personal AI | First Person Labs’ Ken Liu
item.description: Personal AI may matter less as a chatbot than as a private memory layer that follows you everywhere.

item.title: #2582 - Greg Anderson
item.description: A Pacific crossing, lockdown defiance, and war memories lead to one hard question: who gets to use force?

item.title: JRE MMA Show #189 with Tommy McMililen
item.description: Fighting gave one athlete purpose, sobriety, and a life he says he might not otherwise have.

item.title: How Business AI Use is Changing
item.description: Business AI use is rising far faster than costs, as companies switch models to chase better deals.

item.title: Can AI Learn to Improve Itself? | Recursive Self-Improvement
item.description: AI can already speed up AI research, but its biggest weakness is knowing which ideas matter.

item.title: Wonder Is the Antidote to Cynicism (Malcolm Guite) | Ep. 605
item.description: Wonder, not cynicism, can lead people from beauty toward goodness, faith, and a richer sense of home.

item.title: He’s Been Abducted By ALIENS Over 100 Times (And Has Proof!)
item.description: A lifelong experiencer claims aliens harvest human reproductive cells, control minds, and may be preparing to join society.

item.title: Alex Imas & Tyler Cowen | AI Is Moving Fast. Why Isn’t the Economy?
item.description: AI is improving fast, but the economy may be waiting on organizations, workers, and institutions to catch up.

item.title: 5 Questions That Could Reshape AI
item.description: Anthropic’s IPO could become the clearest public test yet of whether AI spending can produce real business value.

item.title: #357 Payne Lindsey - “He Was the First Monster I Ever Really Encountered”
item.description: A true-crime filmmaker becomes an investigator, confronts dangerous suspects, and says a spiritual encounter changed his life.

item.title: 326. Crafting a Vision of Excellence
item.description: A better reason can change not only how you act, but what the action becomes.

item.title: What Breaks When You Scale 10x? | Zipline’s Keller Cliffton
item.description: Every tenfold jump breaks Zipline’s old playbook—and the company expects to make that jump almost every year.

item.title: 7 Things AI-Native Companies Do Differently
item.description: The best AI-native companies are replacing fixed digital teammates with context-rich systems that summon the right workers for each task.

item.title: From the Telephone to Modern Computing | James Gleick
item.description: The telephone’s biggest breakthroughs came from users, accidents, and inventions made without a clear business plan.

item.title: Washington Is Taking Control of AI
item.description: Jensen Huang’s exit is turning a corporate scandal into a new U.S.–China technology crackdown.

item.title: Every Day Is Zero Day | Wiz CTO Ami Luttwak
item.description: AI is shrinking the gap between finding a weakness and using it, forcing defenders to attack themselves every day.

item.title: #2581 - Protect Our Parks 18
item.description: A conspiracy forum, a frozen ship, and a disputed relic all make certainty look surprisingly fragile.

item.title: The Next Era of Games: Mods, Agents, and Infinite Worlds
item.description: AI could turn games from fixed products into worlds players build, remix, and reshape while playing.

item.title: Let's Talk About These Atheist TikToks | Ethan Muse | Last Call Ep. 40
item.description: The episode argues that disbelief may sometimes reflect resistance to God’s demands—not simply a lack of evidence.

item.title: Jensen Huang Is Out. Everything in AI Is Now Up for Grabs.
item.description: NVIDIA’s CEO is out, and his removal could reshape chips, open AI, China policy, and the industry’s financial backbone.

item.title: #356 Joe Kent - Susie Wiles, Stephen Miller, Midterms and the AIPAC Problem
item.description: The episode argues that voters did not abandon Trump—they felt betrayed by wars, lobbyists, and broken promises.

item.title: #2580 - Kenneth Lacovera
item.description: The fossil record reveals a world where dinosaurs ruled for ages, vanished almost instantly, and still shape science today.

item.title: What the Internet Boom Teaches Us About the AI Buildout | Mike Volpi
item.description: AI may be more valuable than the internet—but its boom could still end with fewer winners.

item.title: Wall Street Has No Idea What Anthropic Is Worth
item.description: Anthropic’s IPO may be worth $1.4 trillion, but the market is guessing because almost nobody knows what the company is worth.

item.title: King's Advisor Reveals What the Royal Family Knows About UFOs
item.description: Royal insiders, alleged crash recoveries, psychic encounters, and nuclear shutdowns form a deeply unsettling case for UFO secrecy.

item.title: JRE MMA Show #188 with Paddy Pimblett
item.description: Fighters may gain 35 pounds overnight, start camps at cave raves, and still question whether their best wins would hold today.

item.title: HubSpot’s Co-Founder on Finding Your Next Startup Idea
item.description: The best startup ideas may come from testing fast, solving ignored problems, and knowing when not to use AI.

item.title: Fable 5.2 Is the Best AI Ever. So Why Am I Not Switching Yet?
item.description: Fable 5.2 may be the strongest AI yet, but its biggest weakness is knowing what people actually want.

item.title: #2579 - Gary Sinise
item.description: Supporting veterans, Gary Sinise argues, means standing with people even when you oppose the wars they fought.

item.title: Scott Kupor on Building a16z and Rebuilding the Federal Workforce
item.description: A venture firm built its edge by turning one investor’s job into an entire support system—and government may need the same overhaul.

item.title: Nvidia CEO Admits Affair With Suspected Chinese Spy
item.description: Nvidia’s CEO says he cheated; the bigger question is whether China gained leverage over America’s most important AI company.

item.title: Marian Dogmas, The SSPX, and Leaving Atheism (Ethan Muse) | Ep. 604
item.description: Miracles, Marian doctrine, conversion, the SSPX, and Mormon origins are tied together by one test: authority.
